title: PayJoin v2, tested live
summary: PayJoin part 2: how v2 hides your payment and your IP from the servers that pass the messages, what broke when we tried it live, and where you can help fix it.
share_text: PayJoin v2, tested live: what works, what breaks, and where to contribute. Notes + every resource from the @CodeOrangeDevs Privacy Track
tldr: PayJoin v2 needs no server of your own: a mailbox directory holds encrypted messages and a relay hides your IP address.
Neither server ever touches your bitcoin or can read the payment. Run by two different parties, neither can link sender and receiver.
Live tests mostly failed: silent fallbacks to normal payments, v1/v2 mismatches, and no clear error messages.
The protocol is simple. The wallet experience is the work left to do, and that is where new contributors come in.
